clue.text: Telephoned after the odds leapt up

indicators.note: after places the word for telephoned behind the odds abbreviation

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds offered on a horse at the off
telephoned means rang

explanation.surface: Someone made a phone call once the betting odds had shot up.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to jump suddenly, so its past tense is a synonym for jumped upward.

clue.text: Remove a coat — and the rest!

definitions.text: Remove a coat — and the rest!

parts.words: Remove a coat — and the rest!
parts.note: taking off a layer of paint is one sense, but the exclamation suggests taking off every garment

explanation.surface: Peel away a coat of paint, or every piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripping paint removes a coat, and undressing completely removes every garment too.

clue.text: Runs riot after the beak leaves

parts.note: a ram is the projecting beak on the prow of a warship
leaves of a book are its pages

explanation.surface: Chaos breaks out once the magistrate has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beak' is British slang for a magistrate, which the surface leans on, but here it is a ship's ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on the rampage is to charge about wildly and destructively.

clue.text: To expose a lie it needs hammering home

definitions.text: To expose a lie it needs hammering home

parts.words: To expose a lie it needs hammering home
parts.note: to expose a falsehood is an idiom using a word for a metal pin, and such a pin is hammered in

explanation.surface: Exposing a falsehood requires driving the point in firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose a lie is an idiom with the same word as a metal pin that is driven in with a hammer.

clue.text: Let heats decide those who run

indicators.note: heats that decide are worked out, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Qualifying heats will settle which runners go through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decide' signals that LET and HEATS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Track runners are sportspeople competing in races, the plain sense of those who run.

clue.text: Grudging tribute is often paid to him

definitions.text: Grudging tribute is often paid to him

parts.words: Grudging tribute is often paid to him
parts.note: tribute here is money owed to the state, which people hand over reluctantly to the official collecting it

explanation.surface: A figure whom people praise only reluctantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribute is levied money, and the revenue official receives it from unwilling payers.

clue.text: Praise one in the upper house in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the peer's title is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a peer sitting in the House of Lords, Britain's upper chamber, is a lord

explanation.surface: A peer in the House of Lords is commended during a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol or glorify someone is to praise them highly.

clue.text: Bound to have a prior engagement

definitions.meaning: being already booked means being busy

explanation.definitionFit: Something roped tightly is bound, and someone busy with a prior commitment is unavailable.

clue.text: Appeared to be soundly joined

indicators.note: soundly signals that the word for joined is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: seamed means joined by a seam

explanation.surface: Something looked as though it was firmly fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: To look or give the impression of being something is to appear so.

clue.text: Marine ordered to stay behind

indicators.note: a marine who is ordered about is put in a new order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier from the navy is told not to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a command to the marine, but signals a rearrangement of MARINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger after others leave is to stay put, a direct synonym.

clue.text: An apology for breaking into a dance

definitions.text: An apology for breaking into a dance

parts.words: An apology for breaking into a dance
parts.note: the polite phrase said when interrupting is also the name of a dance where partners may be cut in on

explanation.surface: Someone says sorry for cutting in on a couple dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The polite phrase begging pardon is what one says when interrupting, and an old ballroom dance allowing cutting-in bears the same name.

clue.text: How detectives may collaborate to catch counterfeiters?

definitions.text: How detectives may collaborate to catch counterfeiters?

parts.words: How detectives may collaborate to catch counterfeiters?
parts.note: detectives share information, and when chasing forgers they might also check banknotes against each other

explanation.surface: Police officers pool their findings to catch forgers.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange views or information is the idiom, and detectives checking forged banknotes would literally set them side by side.

clue.text: The height of irritation, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver the word for irritation is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: pique is a feeling of irritation or resentment

explanation.surface: Someone at the very height of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: The summit or highest point of something is its top.

clue.text: Come out with me again and have a drink

indicators.note: again means the shortened word is written twice
out says the letters of the word me are taken away from come

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to go out on a date once more for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out with me' reads as an invitation, but it instructs: remove a word from another; 'out' signals the removal and 'again' the doubling, with 'and have' as link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate beverage made from powdered cacao is a familiar bedtime drink.

clue.text: French priest sought in Lourdes

definitions.meaning: a parish priest in a French village or town
Lourdes is a French pilgrimage town where the sick seek healing

explanation.definitionFit: A curé is a French parish priest, and a healing remedy is what pilgrims to Lourdes hope for.

clue.text: A means of fixing wages

definitions.meaning: a threaded fastener holds things together
old British slang for pay or salary

explanation.definitionFit: A threaded fastener fixes things together, and in British slang it also means salary or pay.

clue.text: Bill is a first name

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: William is a given name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a nickname for William, but it is an invoice, abbreviated as account; it goes at the end even though it leads the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is a male given name, the son of Abraham in the Bible.

clue.text: Shine in languages

parts.note: French is a language spoken in France
Polish is the language of Poland

explanation.surface: Someone excels at speaking foreign tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shine in' reads as 'excel at', but Shine is the definition: a glossy shellac finish for furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy shellac finish on wooden furniture gives it a high sheen.

clue.text: Diverted assets from workers' home and shed

parts.note: a hive is home to worker bees
to doff is to take off, or shed, a garment

explanation.surface: A firm moved money out of its staff housing and a storage hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' suggests employees but means worker bees; 'shed' looks like a hut but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate part of a business and transfer it elsewhere is to split assets away.

clue.text: Examines seals, any broken?

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of seals and any are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: An inspector checks the seals to see if any are broken.
explanation.definitionFit: To study something closely and in detail is to examine it.

clue.text: Fall damaged toe, cried with pain

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters of toe, cried and pain are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: After a tumble someone hurt a toe and yelled in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' looks like a tumble but is a drop in value; 'damaged' rearranges TOE, CRIED and PAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss in value over time, as of a car or currency, is a decline or drop.

clue.text: Turned and fled with detectives in pursuit

indicators.note: in pursuit means the detectives follow behind the word for fled

parts.note: fled means ran
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: A suspect wheeled round and ran off with police chasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like changing direction but means gone sour, like milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off or soured smells rotten, as milk does when it has turned.

clue.text: A dodgy sort of winter sports competition

definitions.text: A dodgy sort of winter sports competition

parts.words: A dodgy sort of winter sports competition
parts.note: dodgy here means involving dodging, as skiers weave between gates on a downhill course

explanation.surface: A ski race of questionable honesty.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski race zigzagging between poles requires skiers to dodge obstacles all the way down.

clue.text: Learner breaks tool making a spindle

indicators.note: breaks means the learner letter splits the tool word open

parts.note: an axe is a chopping tool
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A novice smashes a tool while making a spindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod on which wheels turn is a shaft or spindle.

clue.text: Provide a finale to the second half of the show

parts.note: a finale is the end

indicators.note: the second half of the word show is its last two letters

explanation.surface: Someone supplies a closing scene for the latter part of a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the second half of' takes OW from SHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To give money or a gift that funds something is to provide for it.

clue.text: Circus performer to make an impression

definitions.meaning: a trained sea mammal balancing balls is a classic circus act
to press a stamp into wax leaves an impression

explanation.definitionFit: A balancing marine mammal performs in circuses, and pressing a stamp into wax makes an impression.

clue.text: A student is under alternative examination

indicators.note: is under means the letters for a student sit below the word for alternative in this down clue

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
L for learner, a student

explanation.surface: A pupil is facing a different kind of test.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'under' places A and L beneath OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as opposed to a written paper, is an examination.

clue.text: A span of roguishness

definitions.meaning: a curved structure bridging a gap

explanation.definitionFit: A curved structure spanning an opening, and an adjective for a playfully knowing, mischievous manner.

clue.text: The rapidity with which a famous person loses heart

indicators.note: loses heart means the middle letter of the word for a famous person is removed

parts.note: a celebrity is a famous person

explanation.surface: How fast a star becomes disillusioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' removes B, the central letter of CELEBRITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiftness of movement or action is speed, a formal synonym for rapidity.

clue.text: Fears loss of opener to slips

indicators.note: loss of opener means the first letter of the word for fears is dropped

parts.note: terrors are great fears

explanation.surface: Nervous fielders fear losing an opening batsman to the slips in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opener is a first batsman and slips are fielders; here 'loss of opener' drops T from TERRORS, and slips means mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips are small mistakes or blunders.

clue.text: Break his model into pieces

indicators.note: into pieces says the letters of his and model are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone smashes a model belonging to him.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear down or wreck something is to break it completely.

clue.text: Changes of clothing

definitions.meaning: a shift is a simple loose dress

explanation.definitionFit: Shifts are alterations or changes, and a shift is also a loose straight dress, an item of clothing.
